scope: Exodus 21–24, all 118 public verses. Prior revisions remain unchanged.

source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public Exodus 22:1 maps to Hebrew Exod 21:37; public 22:2–31 maps to Hebrew 22:1–30. Chapters 21, 23, and 24 otherwise align.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial assessments are separate from similarity scores. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Retains divine continuation to Moses and rulings as case instructions.
verses.before: “And these are the judgments that you will set before them:
verses.after: “These are the rulings you are to set before them.
verses.tsw_comparator: “And these are the judgments that you shall set before them:

verses.rationale: Names purchased slavery and male referent, preserving six years and seventh-year release without payment.
verses.before: If you acquire a Hebrew servant, six years he will serve, but in the seventh he will go out free, without payment.
verses.after: If you buy a Hebrew slave, he is to serve for six years. In the seventh year he is to go free, without payment.
verses.tsw_comparator: If you acquire a Hebrew servant, six years he shall serve, but in the seventh he shall go out free, without payment.

verses.rationale: Keeps entry circumstances governing release and the wife’s accompanying departure.
verses.before: If he came in by himself, he will go out by himself. If he was husband of a wife, then his wife will go out with him.
verses.after: If he came in alone, he is to leave alone. If he was married, his wife is to leave with him.
verses.tsw_comparator: If he came in by himself, he shall go out by himself. If he was husband of a wife, then his wife shall go out with him.

verses.rationale: Preserves the ownership claim and forced family separation rather than presenting this as ordinary employment.
verses.before: If his master gave him a wife and she bore him sons or daughters, the wife and her children will belong to her master, and he will go out by himself.
verses.after: If his master gave him a wife and she bore him sons or daughters, the wife and her children belong to her master. He is to leave alone.
verses.tsw_comparator: If his master gave him a wife and she bore him sons or daughters, the wife and her children shall belong to her master, and he shall go out by himself.

verses.rationale: Retains emphatic declaration and all three objects of love; sentence continues to the required action.
verses.before: But if the servant plainly says, ‘I love my master, my wife, and my children; I will not go out free,’
verses.after: But if the slave firmly declares, ‘I love my master, my wife, and my children. I will not go free,’
verses.tsw_comparator: But if the servant plainly says, ‘I love my master, my wife, and my children; I will not go out free,’

verses.rationale: Keeps ha-elohim as God with judicial alternative noted; retains piercing and permanent service without harmonizing to Jubilee.
verses.before: then his master will bring him to God. He will bring him to the door or to the doorpost, and his master will pierce his ear with an awl, and he will serve him permanently.
verses.after: his master is to bring him before God and then bring him to the door or the doorpost. His master is to pierce his ear with an awl, and he will serve him permanently.
verses.tsw_comparator: then his master shall bring him to God. He shall bring him to the door or to the doorpost, and his master shall pierce his ear with an awl, and he shall serve him permanently.

verses.rationale: Keeps daughter-sale and explicit unequal release rule; does not soften female slavery to domestic service.
verses.before: “And if a man sells his daughter as a female servant, she will not go out as the male servants go out.
verses.after: If a man sells his daughter as a slave, she is not to leave as male slaves do.
verses.tsw_comparator: “And if a man sells his daughter as a female servant, she shall not go out as the male servants go out.

verses.rationale: Follows qere lo for himself rather than written not, records both, and retains redemption and betrayal.
verses.before: If she is displeasing in the eyes of her master who designated her for himself, he will let her be redeemed. He will have no authority to sell her to a foreign people, because he has acted treacherously against her.
verses.after: If she displeases the master who designated her for himself, he must allow her to be redeemed. He has no right to sell her to a foreign people, because he has betrayed her.
verses.tsw_comparator: If she is displeasing in the eyes of her master who designated her for himself, he shall let her be redeemed. He shall have no authority to sell her to a foreign people, because he has acted treacherously against her.

verses.rationale: Preserves son designation and daughter-status rights without adding an unstated consent process.
verses.before: If he designates her for his son, he will deal with her according to the rights of daughters.
verses.after: If he designates her for his son, he must treat her according to the rights of daughters.
verses.tsw_comparator: If he designates her for his son, he shall deal with her according to the rights of daughters.

verses.rationale: Keeps three obligations and polygynous setting; chooses traditional marital-rights sense of rare onah with uncertainty noted.
verses.before: If he takes another wife for himself, he will not diminish her food, her clothing, or her marital rights.
verses.after: If he takes another wife, he must not reduce the first woman’s food, clothing, or marital rights.
verses.tsw_comparator: If he takes another wife for himself, he shall not diminish her food, her clothing, or her marital rights.

verses.rationale: Takes three things as preceding obligations and preserves doubled no-payment language.
verses.before: If he does not do these three things for her, she will go out free, without payment of silver.
verses.after: If he does not provide these three things for her, she is to leave without payment, owing no money.
verses.tsw_comparator: If he does not do these three things for her, she shall go out free, without payment of silver.

verses.rationale: Keeps lethal striking and mandatory death sanction; generic victim rendered inclusively.
verses.before: “Whoever strikes a person so that he dies will surely be put to death.
verses.after: Anyone who strikes a person and kills them must be put to death.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Whoever strikes a person so that he dies shall surely be put to death.

verses.rationale: Retains lack of ambush and explicit divine agency instead of replacing both with a secular accident label.
verses.before: But if he did not lie in wait and God allowed it to meet his hand, I will appoint for you a place to which he may flee.
verses.after: But if the person did not lie in wait, and God let it happen at their hand, I will appoint a place where they can flee.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if he did not lie in wait and God allowed it to meet his hand, I will appoint for you a place to which he may flee.

verses.rationale: Keeps deliberate attack with deceitful lethal purpose and removal from altar refuge with execution explicit; avoids making a mere unacted plan the offense.
verses.before: But if a man acts presumptuously against his neighbor to kill him with cunning, you will take him from my altar to die.
verses.after: But if someone deliberately attacks their neighbor to kill them by deceit, take that person even from my altar and put them to death.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if a man acts presumptuously against his neighbor to kill him with cunning, you shall take him from my altar to die.

verses.rationale: Preserves either parent and striking without adding death of the parent as a condition.
verses.before: Whoever strikes his father or his mother will surely be put to death.
verses.after: Anyone who strikes their father or mother must be put to death.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever strikes his father or his mother shall surely be put to death.

verses.rationale: Unfolds sold or found-in-hand alternatives, keeping human theft and both qualifying outcomes.
verses.before: Whoever kidnaps a person, whether he sells that person or the person is found in his hand, will surely be put to death.
verses.after: Anyone who kidnaps a person must be put to death, whether they have sold that person or still hold them in their possession.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever kidnaps a person, whether he sells that person or the person is found in his hand, shall surely be put to death.

verses.rationale: Retains curse rather than reducing the offense to ordinary disagreement with parents.
verses.before: Whoever curses his father or his mother will surely be put to death.
verses.after: Anyone who curses their father or mother must be put to death.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever curses his father or his mother shall surely be put to death.

verses.rationale: Preserves male combatants, two instruments and nonfatal confinement; condition continues into recovery clause.
verses.before: “And if men quarrel and one strikes the other with a stone or with his fist, and he does not die but falls into bed,
verses.after: If men quarrel and one strikes the other with a stone or his fist, and the injured man does not die but is confined to bed,
verses.tsw_comparator: “And if men quarrel and one strikes the other with a stone or with his fist, and he does not die but falls into bed,

verses.rationale: Keeps mobility criterion and remaining obligations so cleared does not imply freedom from compensation.
verses.before: if he rises and walks outside with his staff, then the one who struck him will be cleared. Only he will pay for his loss of time and will surely cause him to be healed.
verses.after: then if he gets up and can walk outside with his staff, the one who struck him is cleared. But he must pay for the injured man’s lost time and ensure his full recovery.
verses.tsw_comparator: if he rises and walks outside with his staff, then the one who struck him shall be cleared. Only he shall pay for his loss of time and shall surely cause him to be healed.

verses.rationale: Keeps male/female enslaved victims, rod, immediate hand image and vengeance without specifying an unstated penalty.
verses.before: If a man strikes his male servant or female servant with a rod and the servant dies under his hand, he will surely be avenged.
verses.after: If a man beats his male or female slave with a rod and the slave dies under his hand, that death must be avenged.
verses.tsw_comparator: If a man strikes his male servant or female servant with a rod and the servant dies under his hand, he shall surely be avenged.

verses.rationale: Retains day-or-two exception and stark monetary-property rationale; does not recast it as benevolent provision or merely financial loss.
verses.before: But if the servant survives a day or two, he will not be avenged, for the servant is his silver.
verses.after: But if the slave survives a day or two, no vengeance is to be taken, because the slave is his money.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if the servant survives a day or two, he shall not be avenged, for the servant is his silver.

verses.rationale: Retains children-coming-out idiom and unspecified harm target; judicial oversight follows biflilim without deciding miscarriage versus surviving premature birth.
verses.before: “And if men fight and strike a pregnant woman so that her children come out, but there is no further harm, he will surely be fined, according to what the woman’s husband lays upon him, and he will pay as the judges determine.
verses.after: If men fight and strike a pregnant woman, and her children come out but no harm occurs, the man responsible must pay a fine as her husband demands, subject to the judges’ decision.
verses.tsw_comparator: “And if men fight and strike a pregnant woman so that her children come out, but there is no further harm, he shall surely be fined, according to what the woman’s husband lays upon him, and he shall pay as the judges determine.

verses.rationale: Keeps unspecified harm and exact reciprocal principle as continuation through the next two verses.
verses.before: But if there is harm, then you will give life for life,
verses.after: But if harm occurs, you must give life for life,
verses.tsw_comparator: But if there is harm, then you shall give life for life,

verses.rationale: Preserves every paired body part and formal legal repetition.
verses.before: eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
verses.after: eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
verses.tsw_comparator: eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,

verses.rationale: Keeps the three injury types and completes the repeated proportional formula.
verses.before: burn for burn, wound for wound, bruise for bruise.
verses.after: burn for burn, wound for wound, bruise for bruise.
verses.tsw_comparator: burn for burn, wound for wound, bruise for bruise.

verses.rationale: Preserves both enslaved sexes, destroyed eye and freedom as required remedy.
verses.before: “And if a man strikes the eye of his male servant or the eye of his female servant and destroys it, he will let the servant go free because of the eye.
verses.after: If a man strikes and destroys the eye of his male or female slave, he must let the slave go free in compensation for the eye.
verses.tsw_comparator: “And if a man strikes the eye of his male servant or the eye of his female servant and destroys it, he shall let the servant go free because of the eye.

verses.rationale: Retains parallel tooth rule without compressing it into the preceding eye injury.
verses.before: And if he knocks out the tooth of his male servant or female servant, he will let the servant go free because of the tooth.
verses.after: If he knocks out the tooth of his male or female slave, he must let the slave go free in compensation for the tooth.
verses.tsw_comparator: And if he knocks out the tooth of his male servant or female servant, he shall let the servant go free because of the tooth.

verses.rationale: Keeps both sexes, animal execution and meat prohibition, with owner status contextualized to this case.
verses.before: “And if an ox gores a man or woman so that the person dies, the ox will surely be stoned and its flesh will not be eaten, but the owner of the ox will be free from guilt.
verses.after: If an ox gores a man or woman to death, the ox must be stoned, and its meat must not be eaten. Its owner is clear of liability.
verses.tsw_comparator: “And if an ox gores a man or woman so that the person dies, the ox shall surely be stoned and its flesh shall not be eaten, but the owner of the ox shall be free from guilt.

verses.rationale: Preserves prior dangerous behavior plus owner warning and failure, distinguishing culpability from the preceding case.
verses.before: But if the ox was accustomed to gore in the past and its owner had been warned but did not restrain it, and it kills a man or woman, the ox will be stoned and its owner also will be put to death.
verses.after: But if the ox was known to gore and its owner had been warned but failed to keep it under control, and it kills a man or woman, the ox must be stoned and its owner must also be put to death.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if the ox was accustomed to gore in the past and its owner had been warned but did not restrain it, and it kills a man or woman, the ox shall be stoned and its owner also shall be put to death.

verses.rationale: Keeps conditional ransom and specified amount instead of automatically commuting the death sanction.
verses.before: If a ransom is imposed upon him, then he will give for the redemption of his life whatever is imposed upon him.
verses.after: If a ransom is imposed on the owner, he must pay whatever is required to redeem his life.
verses.tsw_comparator: If a ransom is imposed upon him, then he shall give for the redemption of his life whatever is imposed upon him.

verses.rationale: Retains explicit younger family categories and equal ruling.
verses.before: Whether it gores a son or gores a daughter, according to this judgment it will be done to him.
verses.after: The same ruling applies if the ox gores a son or daughter.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whether it gores a son or gores a daughter, according to this judgment it shall be done to him.

verses.rationale: Preserves unequal fixed payment to the master, exact thirty shekels and animal death; identifies payer and payee clearly.
verses.before: If the ox gores a male servant or female servant, thirty shekels of silver will be given to the servant’s master, and the ox will be stoned.
verses.after: If the ox gores a male or female slave, its owner must give the slave’s master thirty shekels of silver, and the ox must be stoned.
verses.tsw_comparator: If the ox gores a male servant or female servant, thirty shekels of silver shall be given to the servant’s master, and the ox shall be stoned.

verses.rationale: Keeps opening/digging alternatives and uncovered hazard with both animal types.
verses.before: “And if a man opens a pit, or if a man digs a pit and does not cover it, and an ox or donkey falls into it,
verses.after: If someone opens a pit, or digs one and leaves it uncovered, and an ox or donkey falls into it,
verses.tsw_comparator: “And if a man opens a pit, or if a man digs a pit and does not cover it, and an ox or donkey falls into it,

verses.rationale: Clarifies compensation and transfer of carcass to the paying pit owner.
verses.before: the owner of the pit will make restitution. He will give silver to its owner, and the dead animal will become his.
verses.after: the owner of the pit must make restitution. He must pay the animal’s owner, and the dead animal becomes his.
verses.tsw_comparator: the owner of the pit shall make restitution. He shall give silver to its owner, and the dead animal shall become his.

verses.rationale: Keeps separate division of sale proceeds and carcass without assuming sale of the carcass.
verses.before: And if one man’s ox injures another’s ox so that it dies, they will sell the live ox and divide its silver, and they will also divide the dead animal.
verses.after: If one man’s ox strikes his neighbor’s ox and kills it, they must sell the living ox and divide its price. They must also divide the dead animal.
verses.tsw_comparator: And if one man’s ox injures another’s ox so that it dies, they shall sell the live ox and divide its silver, and they shall also divide the dead animal.

verses.rationale: Preserves known-risk exception, full replacement and carcass disposition.
verses.before: Or if it was known that the ox was accustomed to gore in the past and its owner did not restrain it, he will surely make restitution, ox for ox, and the dead animal will become his.
verses.after: But if the ox was known to gore and its owner failed to keep it under control, he must replace ox for ox, and the dead animal becomes his.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Or if it was known that the ox was accustomed to gore in the past and its owner did not restrain it, he shall surely make restitution, ox for ox, and the dead animal shall become his.

verses.rationale: Binds public verse to Hebrew 21:37; preserves 5/4 distinction and seh species breadth.
verses.before: “If a man steals an ox or a sheep and slaughters it or sells it, he will make restitution of five oxen for the ox and four sheep for the sheep.
verses.after: “If someone steals an ox or an animal from a flock and slaughters or sells it, they must repay five cattle for the ox and four sheep or goats for the flock animal.
verses.tsw_comparator: “If a man steals an ox or a sheep and slaughters it or sells it, he shall make restitution of five oxen for the ox and four sheep for the sheep.

verses.rationale: Makes ambiguous pronoun’s referent explicit as striker in bloodguilt clause; breaking-in covers tunneling image noted selectively.
verses.before: If a thief is found breaking in and is struck so that he dies, there will be no bloodguilt for him.
verses.after: If a thief is caught breaking in and is struck and dies, there is no bloodguilt for the one who struck him.
verses.tsw_comparator: If a thief is found breaking in and is struck so that he dies, there shall be no bloodguilt for him.

verses.rationale: Retains daylight distinction, pronoun openness and forced sale rather than replacing restitution with prison.
verses.before: But if the sun has risen upon him, there will be bloodguilt for him. The thief will surely make restitution. If he has nothing, then he will be sold for his theft.
verses.after: But if the sun has risen on him, there is bloodguilt. A thief must make full restitution. If he has nothing, he is to be sold for what he stole.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if the sun has risen upon him, there shall be bloodguilt for him. The thief shall surely make restitution. If he has nothing, then he shall be sold for his theft.

verses.rationale: Keeps live possession and double restitution distinct from slaughtered/sold penalty.
verses.before: If the stolen animal is found alive in his hand, whether ox, donkey, or sheep, he will make double restitution.
verses.after: If the stolen animal is found alive in his possession, whether an ox, donkey, sheep, or goat, he must repay double.
verses.tsw_comparator: If the stolen animal is found alive in his hand, whether ox, donkey, or sheep, he shall make double restitution.

verses.rationale: Chooses grazing sense of baar and clarifies liable owner’s best produce; exact qere record remains bound.
verses.before: “If a man causes a field or vineyard to be grazed over and lets his livestock loose so that it grazes in another’s field, he will make restitution from the best of his own field and the best of his own vineyard.
verses.after: If someone grazes a field or vineyard and lets their livestock loose to graze in another person’s field, they must make restitution from the best of their own field and vineyard.
verses.tsw_comparator: “If a man causes a field or vineyard to be grazed over and lets his livestock loose so that it grazes in another’s field, he shall make restitution from the best of his own field and the best of his own vineyard.

verses.rationale: Preserves spreading fire, all three loss categories and responsibility of igniter.
verses.before: If fire breaks out and catches in thorns so that stacked grain, standing grain, or a field is consumed, the one who started the fire will surely make restitution.
verses.after: If a fire spreads into thorns and consumes stacked grain, standing grain, or a field, the one who started the fire must make full restitution.
verses.tsw_comparator: If fire breaks out and catches in thorns so that stacked grain, standing grain, or a field is consumed, the one who started the fire shall surely make restitution.

verses.rationale: Makes custody relationship and conditional identification of thief clear.
verses.before: “If a man gives his neighbor silver or goods to keep and it is stolen from the man’s house, if the thief is found, he will make double restitution.
verses.after: If someone entrusts money or goods to a neighbor for safekeeping and they are stolen from the neighbor’s house, the thief must repay double if found.
verses.tsw_comparator: “If a man gives his neighbor silver or goods to keep and it is stolen from the man’s house, if the thief is found, he shall make double restitution.

verses.rationale: Retains God reading of ha-elohim, judicial determination and property seizure idiom; judges alternative explained.
verses.before: If the thief is not found, then the owner of the house will be brought before God to determine whether he has stretched out his hand against his neighbor’s property.
verses.after: If the thief is not found, the householder must come before God to determine whether he has laid hands on his neighbor’s property.
verses.tsw_comparator: If the thief is not found, then the owner of the house shall be brought before God to determine whether he has stretched out his hand against his neighbor’s property.

verses.rationale: Keeps full property list and terse deictic claim; before-God passive leaves human judicial mediation possible, with plural Hebrew verb noted.
verses.before: For every matter of transgression concerning an ox, donkey, sheep, garment, or any lost thing about which one says, ‘This is it,’ the case of both parties will come before God. The one whom God declares guilty will make double restitution to his neighbor.
verses.after: In every dispute over wrongdoing—whether it concerns an ox, a donkey, a sheep or goat, a garment, or any lost thing claimed as ‘This is it!’—both parties’ case must come before God. Whoever is found guilty before God must repay the neighbor double.
verses.tsw_comparator: For every matter of transgression concerning an ox, donkey, sheep, garment, or any lost thing about which one says, ‘This is it,’ the case of both parties shall come before God. The one whom God declares guilty shall make double restitution to his neighbor.

verses.rationale: Retains all animal categories and three unwitnessed loss conditions before oath remedy.
verses.before: If a man gives his neighbor a donkey, ox, sheep, or any animal to keep and it dies, is injured, or is driven away when no one sees,
verses.after: If someone entrusts a donkey, ox, sheep, goat, or any other animal to a neighbor for safekeeping, and it dies, is injured, or is carried off with no witness,
verses.tsw_comparator: If a man gives his neighbor a donkey, ox, sheep, or any animal to keep and it dies, is injured, or is driven away when no one sees,

verses.rationale: Makes keeper and owner distinct, retaining oath and no-payment result for this case.
verses.before: an oath before the LORD will be between them to determine whether he stretched out his hand against his neighbor’s property. Its owner will accept this, and the other will not make restitution.
verses.after: an oath before the LORD is to settle the matter between them, declaring that the keeper has not laid hands on the neighbor’s property. The owner must accept it, and the keeper need not make restitution.
verses.tsw_comparator: an oath before the LORD shall be between them to determine whether he stretched out his hand against his neighbor’s property. Its owner shall accept this, and the other shall not make restitution.

verses.rationale: Preserves explicit theft exception without harmonizing with unwitnessed carrying-off case.
verses.before: But if it was truly stolen from him, he will make restitution to its owner.
verses.after: But if the animal was stolen from the keeper, the keeper must make restitution to its owner.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if it was truly stolen from him, he shall make restitution to its owner.

verses.rationale: Retains physical evidence and exception for predation without inventing witnesses.
verses.before: If it was torn apart, he will bring it as evidence. He will not make restitution for what was torn.
verses.after: If it was torn apart, the keeper must bring it as evidence. No restitution is required for the torn animal.
verses.tsw_comparator: If it was torn apart, he shall bring it as evidence. He shall not make restitution for what was torn.

verses.rationale: Keeps borrowing distinct from safekeeping and owner-absence condition.
verses.before: “If a man borrows an animal from his neighbor and it is injured or dies while its owner is not with it, he will surely make restitution.
verses.after: If someone borrows an animal from a neighbor and it is injured or dies while its owner is absent, the borrower must make full restitution.
verses.tsw_comparator: “If a man borrows an animal from his neighbor and it is injured or dies while its owner is not with it, he shall surely make restitution.

verses.rationale: Chooses hired animal and rental coverage reading of terse clause; terse Hebrew clause and limited certainty acknowledged in note.
verses.before: If its owner is with it, he will not make restitution. If it was hired, the loss is covered by its hire.
verses.after: If its owner is present, no restitution is required. If it was hired, the loss is covered by the hire price.
verses.tsw_comparator: If its owner is with it, he shall not make restitution. If it was hired, the loss is covered by its hire.

verses.rationale: Retains seduction, virginity, unbetrothed status and marriage payment without asserting her consent or changing this into the differently worded rape law.
verses.before: “If a man seduces a virgin who is not betrothed and lies with her, he will surely pay the bride-price for her to become his wife.
verses.after: If a man seduces a virgin who is not pledged in marriage and lies with her, he must pay the bride-price for her to become his wife.
verses.tsw_comparator: “If a man seduces a virgin who is not betrothed and lies with her, he shall surely pay the bride-price for her to become his wife.

verses.rationale: Preserves father’s refusal and continuing payment obligation without supplying the woman’s absent speech.
verses.before: If her father absolutely refuses to give her to him, he will weigh out silver according to the bride-price for virgins.
verses.after: If her father firmly refuses to give her to him, he must still pay an amount equal to the bride-price for virgins.
verses.tsw_comparator: If her father absolutely refuses to give her to him, he shall weigh out silver according to the bride-price for virgins.

verses.rationale: Preserves female form and lethal prohibition without softening or extending it to modern categories.
verses.before: You will not allow a sorceress to live.
verses.after: Do not allow a sorceress to live.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not allow a sorceress to live.

verses.rationale: Makes lies-with sexual sense explicit and retains death sanction.
verses.before: Whoever lies with an animal will surely be put to death.
verses.after: Anyone who has sexual relations with an animal must be put to death.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever lies with an animal shall surely be put to death.

verses.rationale: Preserves herem technical destruction formula and exclusive recipient rather than a vague exclusion.
verses.before: Whoever sacrifices to a god other than the LORD alone will be devoted to destruction.
verses.after: Anyone who sacrifices to gods other than the LORD alone must be devoted to destruction.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever sacrifices to a god other than the LORD alone shall be devoted to destruction.

verses.rationale: Keeps both wronging and oppression grounded in shared experience of foreign residence.
verses.before: “You will not wrong a resident alien or oppress him, for you were resident aliens in the land of Egypt.
verses.after: Do not wrong or oppress a foreigner living among you, because you were foreigners in Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: “You shall not wrong a resident alien or oppress him, for you were resident aliens in the land of Egypt.

verses.rationale: Retains widows and specifically fatherless category, not only children who have lost both parents.
verses.before: You will not afflict any widow or orphan.
verses.after: Do not mistreat any widow or fatherless child.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not afflict any widow or orphan.

verses.rationale: Preserves emphatic mistreatment, cry and certain hearing, using collective plural for the prior protected groups.
verses.before: If you do afflict them and they cry out to me, I will surely hear their cry.
verses.after: If you do mistreat them and they cry out to me, I will surely hear their cry.
verses.tsw_comparator: If you do afflict them and they cry out to me, I will surely hear their cry.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine lethal agency and matching reversal of protected family conditions without moralizing commentary.
verses.before: My anger will burn, and I will kill you with the sword, and your wives will become widows and your children orphans.
verses.after: My anger will burn, and I will kill you with the sword. Your wives will become widows and your children fatherless.
verses.tsw_comparator: My anger will burn, and I will kill you with the sword, and your wives will become widows and your children orphans.

verses.rationale: Preserves poor member scope and broad interest prohibition, not merely excessive interest.
verses.before: “If you lend silver to my people, to the poor among you, you will not be to him like a creditor. You will not impose interest upon him.
verses.after: If you lend money to one of my people who is poor among you, do not act as a creditor toward them. Do not charge them interest.
verses.tsw_comparator: “If you lend silver to my people, to the poor among you, you shall not be to him like a creditor. You shall not impose interest upon him.

verses.rationale: Retains security pledge and exact sunset deadline, continuing into reason.
verses.before: If you take your neighbor’s garment as a pledge, you will return it to him before the sun goes down,
verses.after: If you take your neighbor’s cloak as a pledge, return it before the sun sets,
verses.tsw_comparator: If you take your neighbor’s garment as a pledge, you shall return it to him before the sun goes down,

verses.rationale: Keeps skin, sleep question and divine hearing rooted in graciousness; written/read annotation included in source hash.
verses.before: for that is his only covering; it is his garment for his body. In what will he sleep? And when he cries to me, I will hear, for I am gracious.
verses.after: because it is their only covering, their cloak next to their skin. What else will they sleep in? When they cry out to me, I will hear, because I am gracious.
verses.tsw_comparator: for that is his only covering; it is his garment for his body. In what will he sleep? And when he cries to me, I will hear, for I am gracious.

verses.rationale: Chooses God for elohim with judges alternative noted; preserves parallel divine and human objects.
verses.before: “You will not revile God, and you will not curse a leader among your people.
verses.after: Do not curse God, and do not curse a leader among your people.
verses.tsw_comparator: “You shall not revile God, and you shall not curse a leader among your people.

verses.rationale: Unfolds fullness and tears as produce and liquid yield, noting obscure wording; retains firstborn sons without importing redemption procedure here.
verses.before: You will not delay to offer from the fullness of your harvest and from the flow of your presses. The firstborn of your sons you will give to me.
verses.after: Do not delay giving from your full harvest and the flow of your presses. Give me the firstborn of your sons.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not delay to offer from the fullness of your harvest and from the flow of your presses. The firstborn of your sons you shall give to me.

verses.rationale: Keeps species, mother, seven-day interval and eighth-day giving.
verses.before: You will do likewise with your oxen and sheep. Seven days it will be with its mother; on the eighth day you will give it to me.
verses.after: Do the same with your cattle, sheep, and goats. Let the firstborn stay with its mother for seven days; give it to me on the eighth day.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall do likewise with your oxen and sheep. Seven days it shall be with its mother; on the eighth day you shall give it to me.

verses.rationale: Retains holy identity, field-torn carcass prohibition and dog disposal, without recasting as general dietary advice.
verses.before: You will be holy people to me. Therefore you will not eat flesh torn by animals in the field; you will throw it to the dogs.
verses.after: You are to be holy people for me. Do not eat meat from an animal torn apart in the field; throw it to the dogs.”
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall be holy people to me. Therefore you shall not eat flesh torn by animals in the field; you shall throw it to the dogs.

verses.rationale: Keeps both false report and collusion, retaining hand image and harmful witness rather than gossip alone.
verses.before: “You will not carry a false report. Do not put your hand with the wicked to become a malicious witness.
verses.after: “Do not spread a false report. Do not join hands with a wicked person to be a malicious witness.
verses.tsw_comparator: “You shall not carry a false report. Do not put your hand with the wicked to become a malicious witness.

verses.rationale: Unfolds repeated turning after many as pressure on testimony, preserving separate conduct and judicial clauses.
verses.before: You will not follow the many to do evil, and you will not testify in a dispute by turning aside after the many to distort justice.
verses.after: Do not follow a crowd into wrongdoing. When you testify in a dispute, do not side with the crowd to bend justice.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not follow the many to do evil, and you shall not testify in a dispute by turning aside after the many to distort justice.

verses.rationale: Retains surprising prohibition of partiality toward the poor alongside the later protection of their justice.
verses.before: Nor will you show favoritism to a poor person in his dispute.
verses.after: Do not favor a poor person in a dispute.
verses.tsw_comparator: Nor shall you show favoritism to a poor person in his dispute.

verses.rationale: Keeps enemy, both animals and emphatic return; does not generalize away the hostile relationship.
verses.before: “If you meet your enemy’s ox or donkey wandering away, you will surely return it to him.
verses.after: If you come across your enemy’s ox or donkey wandering away, be sure to take it back to him.
verses.tsw_comparator: “If you meet your enemy’s ox or donkey wandering away, you shall surely return it to him.

verses.rationale: Chooses assistance sense of repeated azav in this difficult construction, retaining hated relationship and shared help; unloading alternative noted.
verses.before: If you see the donkey of one who hates you lying under its load, you will refrain from abandoning him. You will surely release it with him.
verses.after: If you see the donkey of someone who hates you lying under its load, do not leave him without help. Be sure to help him with it.
verses.tsw_comparator: If you see the donkey of one who hates you lying under its load, you shall refrain from abandoning him. You shall surely release it with him.

verses.rationale: Preserves the needy person’s justice, balancing verse 3 without collapsing distinct prohibitions.
verses.before: “You will not distort the justice due to your poor in his dispute.
verses.after: Do not deny a poor person among you justice in a dispute.
verses.tsw_comparator: “You shall not distort the justice due to your poor in his dispute.

verses.rationale: Keeps lethal judicial harm and divine refusal to justify the wicked rather than a general honesty maxim.
verses.before: Keep far from a false matter. Do not kill the innocent or the righteous, for I will not declare the wicked innocent.
verses.after: Keep far from a false charge. Do not kill the innocent or those in the right, because I will not acquit the wicked.
verses.tsw_comparator: Keep far from a false matter. Do not kill the innocent or the righteous, for I will not declare the wicked innocent.

verses.rationale: Preserves sight image and distortion of righteous words with repeated bribe for the causal connection.
verses.before: You will not take a bribe, for a bribe blinds people who see and twists the words of the righteous.
verses.after: Do not accept a bribe. A bribe blinds those who can see and twists the words of those in the right.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not take a bribe, for a bribe blinds those who see and twists the words of the righteous.

verses.rationale: Renders knowing the foreigner’s nephesh as experiential understanding and keeps emphatic yourselves and Egyptian memory.
verses.before: You will not oppress a resident alien. You yourselves know the life of the resident alien, for you were resident aliens in the land of Egypt.
verses.after: Do not oppress a foreigner living among you. You yourselves know what it is like to be a foreigner, because you were foreigners in Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not oppress a resident alien. You yourselves know the life of the resident alien, for you were resident aliens in the land of Egypt.

verses.rationale: Keeps six-year cultivation and gathering as preparation for land release.
verses.before: “Six years you will sow your land and gather its produce.
verses.after: For six years sow your land and gather its produce.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Six years you shall sow your land and gather its produce.

verses.rationale: Preserves seventh-year relinquishment, ordered access for poor and animals, and both perennial crops.
verses.before: But in the seventh you will let it rest and leave it alone, so that the poor of your people may eat, and what they leave the animals of the field may eat. You will do likewise with your vineyard and your olive grove.
verses.after: But in the seventh year let it rest and leave it alone, so the poor among your people can eat from it. The wild animals can eat what they leave. Do the same with your vineyard and olive grove.
verses.tsw_comparator: But in the seventh you shall let it rest and leave it alone, so that the poor of your people may eat, and what they leave the animals of the field may eat. You shall do likewise with your vineyard and your olive grove.

verses.rationale: Keeps the specifically named enslaved woman’s son and foreigner, animal rest and refreshment’s breathing image.
verses.before: Six days you will do your work, but on the seventh day you will cease, so that your ox and donkey may rest, and the son of your female servant and the resident alien may be refreshed.
verses.after: For six days do your work, but stop on the seventh day, so your ox and donkey can rest, and the son of your female slave and the foreigner can catch their breath.
verses.tsw_comparator: Six days you shall do your work, but on the seventh day you shall cease, so that your ox and donkey may rest, and the son of your female servant and the resident alien may be refreshed.

verses.rationale: Chooses cultic invocation for mention in context, retaining the stricter lips prohibition rather than explaining it away.
verses.before: Be careful concerning all that I have said to you. You will not mention the name of other gods; it will not be heard from your mouth.
verses.after: Take care to keep everything I have told you. Do not invoke the names of other gods; do not let them be heard on your lips.
verses.tsw_comparator: Be careful concerning all that I have said to you. You shall not mention the name of other gods; it shall not be heard from your mouth.

verses.rationale: Preserves number, annual cycle and divine recipient before the named festivals.
verses.before: “Three times in the year you will hold a festival for me.
verses.after: Three times a year you are to hold a festival for me.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Three times in the year you shall hold a festival for me.

verses.rationale: Keeps festival name, seven days, Abib, remembered departure and appearing with a gift.
verses.before: You will keep the Festival of Unleavened Bread. Seven days you will eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, at the appointed time in the month of Abib, for in it you came out from Egypt. No one will appear before me empty-handed.
verses.after: Keep the Festival of Unleavened Bread. Eat unleavened bread for seven days, as I commanded you, at the appointed time in the month of Abib, because that was when you came out of Egypt. No one is to appear before me empty-handed.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall keep the Festival of Unleavened Bread. Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, at the appointed time in the month of Abib, for in it you came out from Egypt. No one shall appear before me empty-handed.

verses.rationale: Preserves both distinct agricultural festivals, firstfruits and year-end timing without replacing names with later labels.
verses.before: And the Festival of Harvest, of the firstfruits of your work, what you sow in the field; and the Festival of Ingathering at the going out of the year, when you gather the fruit of your work from the field.
verses.after: Keep the Festival of Harvest with the firstfruits of your work, of what you sow in the field. Also keep the Festival of Ingathering at the year’s end, when you gather the fruit of your work from the field.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the Festival of Harvest, of the firstfruits of your work, what you sow in the field; and the Festival of Ingathering at the going out of the year, when you gather the fruit of your work from the field.

verses.rationale: Preserves explicitly male obligation and Adon YHWH combination, using conventional Lord GOD typography rather than expanding to everyone.
verses.before: Three times in the year all your males will appear before the Lord GOD.
verses.after: Three times a year all your males are to appear before the Lord GOD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Three times in the year all your males shall appear before the Lord GOD.

verses.rationale: Keeps blood, leaven prohibition, specific fat portion and morning deadline without substituting all meat.
verses.before: You will not offer the blood of my sacrifice with anything leavened, and the fat of my festival sacrifice will not remain until morning.
verses.after: Do not offer the blood of my sacrifice with anything leavened. Do not leave the fat of my festival offering overnight until morning.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not offer the blood of my sacrifice with anything leavened, and the fat of my festival sacrifice shall not remain until morning.

verses.rationale: Preserves firstfruits, sanctuary house and exact kid/mother’s-milk restriction without importing later dietary interpretation.
verses.before: The best of the firstfruits of your ground you will bring into the house of the LORD your God. You will not boil a young goat in its mother’s milk.
verses.after: Bring the first of your land’s firstfruits to the house of the LORD your God. Do not boil a young goat in its mother’s milk.
verses.tsw_comparator: The best of the firstfruits of your ground you shall bring into the house of the LORD your God. You shall not boil a young goat in its mother’s milk.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine messenger as angel, guarding and prepared destination, without naming an otherwise unidentified figure.
verses.before: “Look, I am sending a messenger before you to guard you on the way and to bring you to the place that I have prepared.
verses.after: Look, I am sending an angel ahead of you to guard you on the way and bring you to the place I have prepared.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Look, I am sending a messenger before you to guard you on the way and to bring you to the place that I have prepared.

verses.rationale: Preserves no-pardon warning and name-within image without resolving the angel’s identity doctrinally.
verses.before: Be careful before him and listen to his voice. Do not rebel against him, for he will not pardon your transgression, for my name is within him.
verses.after: Be attentive to him and obey his voice. Do not rebel against him, because he will not pardon your rebellion, for my name is within him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Be careful before him and listen to his voice. Do not rebel against him, for he will not pardon your transgression, for my name is within him.

verses.rationale: Keeps messenger’s voice and divine speech linked but distinct, with reciprocal enemy/adversary language.
verses.before: But if you truly listen to his voice and do all that I speak, then I will be an enemy to your enemies and an adversary to your adversaries.
verses.after: If you truly obey his voice and do everything I say, I will be an enemy to your enemies and oppose those who oppose you.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if you truly listen to his voice and do all that I speak, then I will be an enemy to your enemies and an adversary to your adversaries.

verses.rationale: Preserves all six peoples in order and explicit divine destruction rather than a neutral settlement account.
verses.before: For my messenger will go before you and bring you to the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites, and Jebusites, and I will cut them off.
verses.after: My angel will go ahead of you and bring you to the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites, and Jebusites, and I will wipe them out.
verses.tsw_comparator: For my messenger will go before you and bring you to the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites, and Jebusites, and I will cut them off.

verses.rationale: Keeps three prohibitions and emphatic destruction of cult objects, distinguishing pillars from generic idols.
verses.before: “You will not bow down to their gods or serve them or do according to their deeds, but you will utterly tear them down and completely shatter their pillars.
verses.after: Do not bow down to their gods, serve them, or imitate their practices. You must tear them down completely and smash their sacred pillars.
verses.tsw_comparator: “You shall not bow down to their gods or serve them or do according to their deeds, but you shall utterly tear them down and completely shatter their pillars.

verses.rationale: Retains source shift from he will bless to I will remove instead of silently harmonizing the speaker’s grammar.
verses.before: You will serve the LORD your God, and he will bless your bread and your water, and I will remove sickness from your midst.
verses.after: Serve the LORD your God, and he will bless your bread and water. I will remove sickness from among you.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall serve the LORD your God, and he will bless your bread and your water, and I will remove sickness from your midst.

verses.rationale: Keeps reproductive and lifespan promises in their addressed land setting, without making present-day medical guarantees.
verses.before: None will miscarry or be barren in your land. I will fulfill the number of your days.
verses.after: No one in your land will miscarry or be barren. I will give you the full number of your days.
verses.tsw_comparator: None shall miscarry or be barren in your land. I will fulfill the number of your days.

verses.rationale: Preserves divine terror, confusion and literal backs image as defeat rather than removing violent agency.
verses.before: “I will send my terror before you and throw into confusion all the people among whom you come, and I will make all your enemies turn their backs to you.
verses.after: I will send my terror ahead of you and throw all the peoples you encounter into confusion. I will make all your enemies turn their backs to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: “I will send my terror before you and throw into confusion all the people among whom you come, and I will make all your enemies turn their backs to you.

verses.rationale: Retains hornet image and three peoples in source order; does not settle literal insect versus figurative agent.
verses.before: I will send the hornet before you, and it will drive out the Hivite, the Canaanite, and the Hittite from before you.
verses.after: I will send the hornet ahead of you, and it will drive out the Hivites, Canaanites, and Hittites before you.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will send the hornet before you, and it will drive out the Hivite, the Canaanite, and the Hittite from before you.

verses.rationale: Keeps one-year limitation and both consequences of sudden depopulation.
verses.before: I will not drive them out from before you in one year, lest the land become desolate and the wild animals multiply against you.
verses.after: I will not drive them out before you in a single year, or the land would become desolate and wild animals would multiply against you.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will not drive them out from before you in one year, lest the land become desolate and the wild animals multiply against you.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated gradual expulsion, population growth and possession rather than smoothing into peaceful migration.
verses.before: Little by little I will drive them out from before you, until you become fruitful and possess the land.
verses.after: Little by little I will drive them out before you, until you have grown in number and can take possession of the land.
verses.tsw_comparator: Little by little I will drive them out from before you, until you become fruitful and possess the land.

verses.rationale: Keeps all four geographic markers, covenantal handing over and human expulsion; identifies seas and River selectively in note.
verses.before: I will set your border from the Sea of Reeds to the Sea of the Philistines, and from the wilderness to the River, for I will give the inhabitants of the land into your hand, and you will drive them out from before you.
verses.after: I will set your borders from the Sea of Reeds to the sea of the Philistines, and from the wilderness to the River. I will give the land’s inhabitants into your hands, and you will drive them out before you.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will set your border from the Sea of Reeds to the Sea of the Philistines, and from the wilderness to the River, for I will give the inhabitants of the land into your hand, and you shall drive them out from before you.

verses.rationale: Preserves covenant term and both prohibited partners rather than reducing it to friendship.
verses.before: You will make no covenant with them or with their gods.
verses.after: Do not make a covenant with them or with their gods.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall make no covenant with them or with their gods.

verses.rationale: Keeps exclusion, stated religious rationale and trap image without contemporary political application.
verses.before: They will not live in your land, lest they cause you to sin against me, for if you serve their gods, it will surely become a snare to you.”
verses.after: They must not live in your land, or they will lead you to sin against me. If you serve their gods, it will become a snare for you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: They shall not live in your land, lest they cause you to sin against me, for if you serve their gods, it will surely become a snare to you.”

verses.rationale: Names the continuing divine speaker from context for clear chapter entry; retains four named men, seventy elders and distance requirement.
verses.before: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Come up to the LORD—you and Aaron, Nadab, and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel—and bow down at a distance.
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses, “Come up to the LORD—you, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy of Israel’s elders—and bow down at a distance.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Come up to the LORD—you and Aaron, Nadab, and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel—and bow down at a distance.

verses.rationale: Preserves distinct access restrictions for Moses, accompanying leaders and people, including third-person Moses in direct speech.
verses.before: Moses alone will come near to the LORD, but the others will not come near, and the people will not come up with him.”
verses.after: Moses alone is to approach the LORD. The others must not approach, and the people must not come up with him.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses alone shall come near to the LORD, but the others shall not come near, and the people shall not come up with him.”

verses.rationale: Keeps words and rulings as paired categories and unified response, connecting rulings to 21:1.
verses.before: Moses came and told the people all the words of the LORD and all the ordinances. And all the people answered with one voice and said, “All the words that the LORD has spoken we will do.”
verses.after: Moses went and told the people all the LORD’s words and all the rulings. The whole people answered with one voice, “We will do everything the LORD has said.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses came and told the people all the words of the LORD and all the ordinances. And all the people answered with one voice and said, “All the words that the LORD has spoken we will do.”

verses.rationale: Preserves written record, early morning, altar location and repeated twelve linking pillars to tribes.
verses.before: Moses wrote down all the words of the LORD. He rose early in the morning and built an altar at the foot of the mountain, and twelve pillars, according to the twelve tribes of Israel.
verses.after: Moses wrote down all the LORD’s words. Early the next morning he built an altar at the foot of the mountain and set up twelve pillars for the twelve tribes of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: And Moses wrote down all the words of the LORD. He rose early in the morning and built an altar at the foot of the mountain, and twelve pillars, according to the twelve tribes of Israel.

verses.rationale: Keeps young men as actual agents rather than importing priests, with two offering types and bulls explicit; peace offerings matches 20:24.
verses.before: And he sent young men of the people of Israel, who offered burnt offerings and sacrificed offerings of well-being to the LORD, oxen.
verses.after: He sent young Israelite men, who offered burnt offerings and sacrificed bulls as peace offerings to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he sent young men of the people of Israel, who offered burnt offerings and sacrificed offerings of well-being to the LORD, oxen.

verses.rationale: Preserves equal blood division, basins and vigorous zaraq action rather than a purely symbolic description.
verses.before: Moses took half of the blood and put it in basins, and half of the blood he threw against the altar.
verses.after: Moses put half the blood into basins and splashed the other half against the altar.
verses.tsw_comparator: And Moses took half of the blood and put it in basins, and half of the blood he threw against the altar.

verses.rationale: Renders sefer as document, retains covenant and audible reading, and keeps both do and hear/obey in their order.
verses.before: Then he took the book of the covenant and read it in the hearing of the people. And they said, “All that the LORD has spoken we will do, and we will hear.”
verses.after: He took the covenant document and read it aloud to the people. They said, “We will do everything the LORD has said, and we will obey.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he took the book of the covenant and read it in the hearing of the people. And they said, “All that the LORD has spoken we will do, and we will hear.”

verses.rationale: Preserves actual blood on people, covenant-making and dependence on preceding words without adding later sacramental interpretation.
verses.before: Moses took the blood and threw it on the people and said, “See—the blood of the covenant that the LORD has cut with you in keeping with all these words.”
verses.after: Moses took the blood and splashed it on the people. “Here is the blood of the covenant the LORD has made with you on the basis of all these words,” he said.
verses.tsw_comparator: And Moses took the blood and threw it on the people and said, “See—the blood of the covenant that the LORD has cut with you in accordance with all these words.”

verses.rationale: Retains repeated names and seventy rather than compressing the party to the leaders.
verses.before: Then Moses and Aaron, Nadab, and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel went up,
verses.after: Moses went up with Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy of Israel’s elders.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Moses and Aaron, Nadab, and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel went up,

verses.rationale: Preserves direct seeing and feet, comparative not exact pavement description, and sky clarity; ancient stone identification noted.
verses.before: and they saw the God of Israel. Under his feet there was something like a pavement of sapphire stone, like the very heavens for clearness.
verses.after: They saw the God of Israel. Beneath his feet was something like a pavement of sapphire, as clear as the sky itself.
verses.tsw_comparator: and they saw the God of Israel. Under his feet there was something like a pavement of sapphire stone, like the very heavens for clearness.

verses.rationale: Keeps withheld hand, repeated seeing and meal without importing an explanation of how the vision was possible.
verses.before: And he did not stretch out his hand against the chief men of the people of Israel; they saw God, and they ate and drank.
verses.after: He did not lay his hand on these leaders of Israel. They beheld God, and they ate and drank.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he did not stretch out his hand against the chief men of the people of Israel; they saw God, and they ate and drank.

verses.rationale: Retains stay, stone tablets, instruction/commandment pairing, divine writing and purpose to teach the people, making the pronoun’s referent clear without asserting a second document.
verses.before: The LORD said to Moses, “Come up to me on the mountain and remain there, and I will give you the tablets of stone, with the instruction and the commandment that I have written for their teaching.”
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses, “Come up to me on the mountain and stay there. I will give you the stone tablets, with the instruction and commandment I have written to teach the people.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to Moses, “Come up to me on the mountain and remain there, and I will give you the tablets of stone, with the instruction and the commandment that I have written for their teaching.”

verses.rationale: Preserves Joshua’s attendant role and singular Moses ascent rather than specifying Joshua’s unstated stopping point.
verses.before: So Moses rose with Joshua his assistant, and Moses went up into the mountain of God.
verses.after: Moses set out with Joshua his attendant, and Moses went up the mountain of God.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Moses rose with Joshua his assistant, and Moses went up into the mountain of God.

verses.rationale: Uses pluperfect for departure instruction and keeps plural return, named delegated authorities and dispute access.
verses.before: And he said to the elders, “Wait here for us until we return to you. See, Aaron and Hur are with you; whoever has a dispute may go to them.”
verses.after: He had told the elders, “Wait here for us until we return to you. Aaron and Hur are here with you; anyone with a dispute should go to them.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said to the elders, “Wait here for us until we return to you. See, Aaron and Hur are with you; whoever has a dispute may go to them.”

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated ascent and covering cloud instead of compressing the narrative sequence.
verses.before: Then Moses went up on the mountain, and the cloud covered the mountain.
verses.after: Moses went up the mountain, and the cloud covered it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Moses went up on the mountain, and the cloud covered the mountain.

verses.rationale: Preserves glory dwelling, six-day covering and seventh-day call with divine subject recovered from context.
verses.before: The glory of the LORD settled on Mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it six days; on the seventh day he called to Moses out of the midst of the cloud.
verses.after: The glory of the LORD settled on Mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it for six days. On the seventh day he called to Moses from within the cloud.
verses.tsw_comparator: The glory of the LORD settled on Mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it six days; on the seventh day he called to Moses out of the midst of the cloud.

verses.rationale: Keeps Israelite viewpoint and explicit fire comparison rather than declaring ordinary combustion.
verses.before: Now the appearance of the glory of the LORD was like a consuming fire on the top of the mountain in the sight of the sons of Israel.
verses.after: To the Israelites, the glory of the LORD looked like a consuming fire on the mountain’s summit.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the appearance of the glory of the LORD was like a consuming fire on the top of the mountain in the sight of the sons of Israel.

verses.rationale: Retains cloud entry, repeated ascent and both forty-day and forty-night duration.
verses.before: Moses entered the midst of the cloud and went up on the mountain. And Moses was on the mountain forty days and forty nights.
verses.after: Moses entered the cloud and went up the mountain. He stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses entered the midst of the cloud and went up on the mountain. And Moses was on the mountain forty days and forty nights.
